headline: Tony Trades Away the Points That Could Have Beaten Stilly

week16.method: Frozen other starters and actual opponent; Hall scenario removes both acquired assets (Cooper benched); Cooper scenarios retain trade. Warren substitution hindsight, not pregame optimal.

sources.finding: Hall averaged 19.2 touches, 103 scrimmage yards since Week5
November15 Watson season-ending shoulder surgery announced before trade
Flacco first start December, later development
Week16 Hall 191 scrimmage yards two rushing TDs
Cooper 265 receiving yards, 11 catches, two TDs
Pregame ranks Kamara RB5, Etienne RB9, Hall RB16, Warren RB27; Diggs WR6, Kupp WR10, Cooper WR20. Actual lineup defensible, alternatives hindsight.

publicationDraft: Tony exchanged Hall for Etienne and Cooper, a defensible consolidation of value at the time. Cleveland had already lost Watson, but Flacco's arrival transformed Cooper's outlook. On Christmas Eve, Hall scored 37.10 for Stew while Etienne supplied Tony just 4.60. Retaining Hall would have left Tony 0.58 short of beating Stilly. Yet Tony had an even bigger weapon: Cooper's 48 points sat on his bench. Starting him over Kupp would have reversed the result. Pregame rankings favored Kupp, so this was not an obvious blunder at kickoff. Tony had the ammunition; the lineup never fired.
